# Set Up
```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#Load packages
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(moments)
library(readxl)
library(dunn.test)
library(gt)
library(paletteer)
library(tinytex)
library(lubridate)
library(viridis)
library(vcdExtra)
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)
library(gridExtra)
#Load in egrid 2023 data
#Only load in sheet 3
#This is raw data on electricity generators in the U.S.

egrid_2023 <- read_xlsx("egrid2023_data.xlsx",
                        sheet = 3)

```

# Data Wrangling

```{r}
#view(egrid_2023)
#add underscore to column names for coding
#first, create a function to add underscore

inject_underscore <- function(df) {
  names(df) <- gsub(" ", "_", names(df))
  return(df)
}

#next, operate function on data frame
egrid_2023 <- inject_underscore(egrid_2023)

colnames(egrid_2023)[colnames(egrid_2023) == 'Generator_nameplate_capacity_(MW)'] <-
  'Generator_nameplate_capacity_MW'

#remove first row, repetitive names
egrid_2023[-c(1), ]
#Both states in same dataset
combined_egrid_2023 <- egrid_2023 %>% 
  filter(Plant_state_abbreviation == c("CA", "TX"))

#Create summary

class(combined_egrid_2023$Generator_nameplate_capacity_MW)

combined_egrid_2023$Generator_nameplate_capacity_MW <-
  as.numeric(combined_egrid_2023$Generator_nameplate_capacity_MW)

combined_egrid_2023$`Generator_annual_net_generation_(MWh)` <-
  as.numeric(combined_egrid_2023$`Generator_annual_net_generation_(MWh)`)

fig2_summary <- combined_egrid_2023 %>% 
  group_by(Plant_state_abbreviation) %>% 
  summarize(Nameplate_Capacity =
              sum(Generator_nameplate_capacity_MW, na.rm = TRUE),
            Annual_Generation = 
              sum(`Generator_annual_net_generation_(MWh)`, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

fig2_summary
```

# Visualize electricity capacity and annual generation in TX and CA in 2023

```{r fig.height=6, warning=FALSE}

state_colors <- c("CA" = "pink", "TX" = "lightblue")

# Plot for Nameplate Capacity

graph_nc <- ggplot(fig2_summary, aes(x = Plant_state_abbreviation, 
                                     y = Nameplate_Capacity, 
                                     fill = Plant_state_abbreviation)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Nameplate Capacity and Annual Generation in California and Texas in 2023",
       y = "Nameplate Capacity (MW)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = state_colors)+
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Plot for Annual Generation
graph_generation<- ggplot(fig2_summary, aes(x = Plant_state_abbreviation, 
                                            y = Annual_Generation, 
                                            fill = Plant_state_abbreviation)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(y = "Annual Generation (MWh)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = state_colors)+
    theme(legend.position = "none")

grid.arrange(graph_nc, graph_generation, ncol = 2)

```


# Data Wrangling

```{r}
# Define colors for states
state_colors <- c("CA" = "pink", "TX" = "lightblue")

# Scale Annual Generation for secondary y-axis visualization
scale_factor <- max(fig2_summary$Nameplate_Capacity) / max(fig2_summary$Annual_Generation)

# Create the plot
graph_combined <- ggplot(fig2_summary, aes(x = Plant_state_abbreviation)) +
  # Nameplate Capacity Bars
  #geom_bar(aes(y = Nameplate_Capacity, fill = Plant_state_abbreviation), 
           #stat = "identity", position = "dodge", width = 0.4, alpha = 0.7) +
  # Annual Generation Bars (scaled)
  geom_bar(aes(y = Annual_Generation, fill = Plant_state_abbreviation), 
           stat = "identity", position = "dodge", width = 0.4, alpha = 0.4) +
  # Left Y-Axis
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Nameplate Capacity (MW)",
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / scale_factor, name = "Annual Generation (MWh)", 
                        labels = scales::comma)
  ) +
  labs(title = "Nameplate Capacity and Annual Generation 
       in California and Texas (2023)",
       x = "State") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = state_colors) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", text = element_text(size = 14))

# Print the combined graph
print(graph_combined)
```

```{r}
fig2_summary_long <- fig2_summary %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Nameplate_Capacity, Annual_Generation),
               names_to = "Metric",
               values_to = "Value")

# **Improved Scaling Factor**
scale_factor <- max(fig2_summary$Annual_Generation) / max(fig2_summary$Nameplate_Capacity)

# Adjust data to properly scale both metrics
fig2_summary_long <- fig2_summary_long %>%
  mutate(Value_Scaled = ifelse(Metric == "Annual_Generation", Value / scale_factor, Value))

fig2_summary_long <- fig2_summary_long %>%
  mutate(Value_Scaled = ifelse(Metric == "Annual_Generation", Value / scale_factor, Value),
         Label = case_when(
           Plant_state_abbreviation == "CA" & Metric == "Nameplate_Capacity" ~ "CA Capacity",
           Plant_state_abbreviation == "TX" & Metric == "Nameplate_Capacity" ~ "TX Capacity",
           Plant_state_abbreviation == "CA" & Metric == "Annual_Generation" ~ "CA Generation",
           Plant_state_abbreviation == "TX" & Metric == "Annual_Generation" ~ "TX Generation"
         ))

graph_combined <- ggplot(fig2_summary_long, aes(x = Label, 
                                                y = Value_Scaled, 
                                                fill = Plant_state_abbreviation)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), width = 0.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Nameplate Capacity (MW)", 
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . * scale_factor, name = "Annual Generation (MWh)", labels = scales::comma)
  ) +
  labs(title = "Nameplate Capacity and Annual Generation
       in California and Texas (2023)",
       x = "State and Metric") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = state_colors) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none", 
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 14),  # Straight, readable x-axis labels
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),  # Increase y-axis label size
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16),  # Make axis title larger
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),  # Make left y-axis title larger
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),  # Enhance title
    text = element_text(size = 14)  # Increase overall text size
  )

# Print the combined graph
print(graph_combined)

```
```{r}
# Reshape data to long format
fig2_summary_long <- fig2_summary %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Nameplate_Capacity, Annual_Generation),
               names_to = "Metric",
               values_to = "Value")

# Define colors for Capacity and Generation (instead of states)
metric_colors <- c("Capacity" = "lightblue", "Generation" = "pink")

# **Improved Scaling Factor**
scale_factor <- max(fig2_summary$Annual_Generation) / max(fig2_summary$Nameplate_Capacity)

# Adjust data to properly scale both metrics
fig2_summary_long <- fig2_summary_long %>%
  mutate(Value_Scaled = ifelse(Metric == "Annual_Generation", Value / scale_factor, Value))

# **Set proper factor levels for grouping by state**
fig2_summary_long$Metric <- factor(fig2_summary_long$Metric, 
                                   levels = c("Nameplate_Capacity", "Annual_Generation"),
                                   labels = c("Capacity", "Generation"))

# Create the plot with **grouped bars by state**
graph_combined <- ggplot(fig2_summary_long, aes(x = Plant_state_abbreviation, 
                                                y = Value_Scaled, 
                                                fill = Metric)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.6), width = 0.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Nameplate Capacity (MW)", 
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . * scale_factor, name = "Annual Generation (MWh)", labels = scales::comma)
  ) +
  labs(title = "Nameplate Capacity and Annual Generation
       in California and Texas (2023)",
       x = "State",
       caption =
"This graph shows the total installed nameplate capacity and annual 
electricity generation in Texas and California in 2023. 

The graph illustrates that both annual electricity generation and capacity
are higher in Texas than in California. Annual electricity generated in Texas 
in 2023 is more than two times of generation in California.") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = metric_colors) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom", 
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14),  # No rotation, as only two labels (CA, TX)
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),  # Increase y-axis label size
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16),  # Make axis title larger
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),  # Make left y-axis title larger
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18),  # Enhance title
    text = element_text(size = 14),
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)# Increase overall text size
  )

ggsave(filename="Figure 2.jpg", 
       plot=graph_combined)

# Print the combined graph
print(graph_combined)
```
